note: The SWEPT PICK and the ladder it was measured on. tools/tune_baselines.nim --sweep replays a bounded matrix over this ladder and prints every candidate's margin; --check re-plays the ladder with the shipped constants and fails if either the constants or the numbers below have drifted. tests/test_snake_control.nim asserts the same thing through src/snake/engine.nim's ladderTotals, which is the single implementation both use.

ladder.why: Each seed is played once per seating, so every baseline occupies each spawn anchor the same number of times. The four anchors are not equally good: on an unmirrored ladder two IDENTICAL players score 0.222 apart, and any margin read off it is mostly seat position.

sweep.why: forager's other five knobs are its CHARACTER (always hungry, tight on space, cheap on risk) and are the design note's: it is the player a champion should be able to beat, so tuning it for the margin would measure the wrong thing. Its spaceWeight is swept because that one knob decides how greedy it really is. Every row is printed by `tune_baselines.nim --sweep`, which ci.yml runs on every push.

measured.comment: Recorded from the swept pick on the seat-mirrored ladder, where an identical pair scores exactly 0.0. coil takes all three modules (royale +999, geese +2666, tron +667 permille) for an overall margin of +0.1805 mean score per seat. The design note's claimed [+0.30,+1.20] band is not reachable anywhere in the swept matrix -- the best candidate is this one. These integers are the regression pin: any change to the rules, the scoring or either baseline moves them.
